text: That morning: Holmes asks whether they could see over the rooms at Stoke Moran unknown to her stepfather
why: Holmes asks at ¶76 whether they could see the rooms at Stoke Moran 'to-day' without the stepfather's knowledge, and the scene is set in the early morning.

text: Does Dr. Roylott know that Helen has gone to Holmes?
why: A plain question the story gives reason to ask: Helen left before six, is secretive, says she has no one to turn to, and is afraid of the stepfather, whose knowledge of her visit is unstated.

text: Does Dr. Roylott know that Helen has gone to Holmes? — he does not know
why: Phrased as a possibility, not a stated fact. Helen left secretly at dawn and Holmes asks about seeing the rooms unknown to the stepfather, so a reader has reason to consider that he does not know.

text: Does Dr. Roylott know that Helen has gone to Holmes? — he has found out
why: Phrased as a possibility. The story shows the stepfather as violent and controlling and Helen as fearful and shielding him, so a reader has reason to wonder whether he has learned of her visit. The story does not state or imply that he has.
